title: mi_fifo Module
content_markdown: This is a module which provides a FIFO transport layer implementation for Management Interface. It receives the command over a FIFO file and returns the output through the reply\_fifo specified.
overview: This is a module which provides a FIFO transport layer implementation for Management Interface. It receives the command over a FIFO file and returns the output through the reply\_fifo specified.
how_it_works: The module checks every 30 seconds if the FIFO file exists, and if it was deleted, it recreates it. If one wants to force the fifo file recreation, it should send a SIGHUP signal to the MI process PID.

exported_parameters.name: fifo_name
exported_parameters.description: The name of the FIFO file to be created for listening and reading external commands.
exported_parameters.notes: Starting with Linux kernel 4.19, processes can no longer read from FIFO files that are saved in directories with sticky bits (such as /tmp) and are not owned by the same user the process runs with. This prevents external tools (such as opensips-cli) from running MI commands using a different user (a Permissions denied error is triggered). If you are getting this error while trying to use opensips-cli, you can fix it by either store the fifo file in a non-sticky bit directory (such as /run/opensips), or disable the fifo protection using sysctl fs.protected_fifos = 0 (NOT RECOMMENDED).

exported_parameters.name: fifo_mode
exported_parameters.description: Permission to be used for creating the listening FIFO file. It follows the UNIX conventions.

exported_parameters.name: fifo_group
exported_parameters.description: Group to be used for creating the listening FIFO file.

exported_parameters.name: fifo_user
exported_parameters.description: User to be used for creating the listening FIFO file.

exported_parameters.name: reply_dir
exported_parameters.description: Directory to be used for creating the reply FIFO files.

exported_parameters.name: pretty_printing
exported_parameters.description: Indicates whether the JSONRPC responses sent through MI should be pretty-printed or not.

exported_parameters.name: trace_destination
exported_parameters.description: Trace destination as defined in the tracing module. Currently the only tracing module is proto_hep. This is where traced mi messages will go.
exported_parameters.notes: WARNING: A tracing module must be loaded in order for this parameter to work. (for example proto_hep).

exported_parameters.name: trace_bwlist
exported_parameters.description: Filter traced mi commands based on a blacklist or a whitelist. trace_destination must be defined for this parameter to have any purpose. Whitelists can be defined using 'w' or 'W', blacklists using 'b' or 'B'. The type is separate by the actual blacklist by ':'. The mi commands in the list must be separated by ','.
exported_parameters.example_code:
## blacklist ps and which mi commands
## all the other commands shall be traced
modparam("mi_fifo", "trace_bwlist", "b: ps, which")
## allow only sip_trace mi command
## all the other commands will not be traced
modparam("mi_fifo", "trace_bwlist", "w: sip_trace")
exported_parameters.notes: Defining a blacklists means all the commands that are not blacklisted will be traced. Defining a whitelist means all the commands that are not whitelisted will not be traced. WARNING: One can't define both a whitelist and a blacklist. Only one of them is allowed. Defining the parameter a second time will just overwrite the first one. WARNING: A tracing module must be loaded in order for this parameter to work. (for example proto_hep).
